style.summary:
style of A: Minimal and supportive, with steady Mm-hmm and Yeah responses.
style of B: Explanatory and confident, using I think and you could to present an idea.

A: A's measured Mm-hmm replies signal evaluation, so B has to earn each step.
A's Right and Yeah let A control the pace without saying much.
A's short tone puts A in the listener's seat, deciding when B's explanation is enough.
B: B's confident I think framing presents B as the expert behind the proposed method.
B's you could phrasing turns the proposal into a suggestion A has to consider.
B's explanatory tone carries the conversation through its whole length.

A: A's Mm-hmm replies are supportive, which means B's explanation is accepted, and that gives B the authority.
A's short Right and Yeah are agreement tokens, so the pace is effectively set by B, who is talking the whole time.
A's role as evaluator depends on B's explanation, so B controls what A has to judge.
B: B's I think framing is a hedge, and A's continued listening keeps A in control of whether the idea is adopted.
B's you could is only a suggestion, so A decides whether the method is used.
B's explanation is cut off, so A is the one who determines whether it is finished.

content.summary:
content of A: Responds with acknowledgments and does not add technical content.
content of B: Proposes a method that uses a noise estimate and smoothing based on the signal-to-noise ratio.

A: A's prompts draw out B's method through acknowledgments, which makes A the one who unlocks the substance.
The method B describes depends on a noise estimate A would supply, so A holds control over the data.
A's neutral acknowledgments leave the method in B's frame, and A can accept or reject it at will.
B: B supplies the substance: the envelope, the noise estimate, and the smoothing idea.
B's signal-to-noise reasoning is the core technical content the exchange is about.
B's description of when to use stronger smoothing decides which method the conversation considers.

A: A's prompts are only Mm-hmm, so B's explanation drives the exchange and gives B the stronger position.
A supplies data for the noise estimate only if B's method calls for it, so B determines what A has to provide.
A's neutral acknowledgments do not decide anything, because B has already set the frame B wants used.
B: B's method is only a proposal, and A's acceptance or rejection decides whether it matters.
The signal-to-noise idea is B's suggestion that A can ignore, so A controls the content.
B's description of stronger smoothing is cut off, so A decides how much of the method is discussed.

coordination.summary:
coordination of A: Gives backchannels that keep B talking, shaping the pace without holding the floor.
coordination of B: Holds the floor for almost the entire exchange and ends mid-sentence.

A: A's backchannels signal when B should continue, which gives A timing control.
A's brief turns leave B to fill the silence, which means B carries the exchange.
A decides when the exchange has gone far enough by withholding a fuller response.
B: B holds the floor for almost the entire exchange.
B drives the explanation forward and decides how far it goes.
B's unfinished you could you could shows B controls the cutoff point.

A: A's backchannels are passive, so B's extended turns give B the timing control in practice.
A's Mm-hmm signals do not steer the conversation, because B decides whether and when to continue.
A's brief turns leave B filling silence, which lets B decide what is said.
B: B holds the floor only because A lets the explanation run, so A decides its length.
B's extended turns respond to A's cues, so A sets the rhythm of the exchange.
B's cutoff is the natural end of a turn, and A chooses whether to take the next one.

engagement.summary:
engagement of A: Shows attention through steady backchannels and close listening.
engagement of B: Explains with an example and is invested in the idea, but does not ask for A's view.

A: A's active listening makes A the one whose understanding B has to win over.
A's Right and Yeah show A is following closely.
A's consistent attention throughout gives A a steady role in the exchange.
B: B is fully invested in explaining the method with an example.
B's extended explanation shows strong personal interest in the idea.
B's description of the signal-to-noise idea is the most engaged content of the exchange.

A: A's listening is passive, and B's extended investment in the idea shows B has the stronger stake.
A's Right and Yeah are polite signals rather than deep involvement, so B's stake outweighs them.
A's consistency is a shallow kind of attention, while B's engagement drives the discussion.
B: B's investment is in a proposal A can accept or reject, so A's judgment is the one that matters.
B's explanation is engaged but does not ask A's view, so B is not establishing shared ground.
B's signal-to-noise idea is only a suggestion that A's listening will ultimately test.
